title: How a speech-to-speech agent skips the text step
subtitle: Audio and video stream over one session to a native audio model that hears, calls tools and talks back.
hook: One websocket replaces three models: speech goes in and comes out as audio, never routed through text.

sources.title: Can Your Agent Hear You Now? Building Live Voice Agents with Gemini
sources.speaker: Thor Schaeff

sources.title: Voice Agents Can Just Do Things
sources.speaker: Charlie Guo

nodes.label: Speaker
nodes.detail: A person talking to the agent with a microphone and, optionally, a camera. In the demo the model read the word on the speaker's sweatshirt.
nodes.tradeoff: The user can barge in and interrupt the model mid-reply, for example when the DJ agent talks too long.

nodes.label: Media framework
nodes.detail: Moves the user's real-time audio and video to the Live API and plays the reply. Google points builders to partners such as LiveKit and Pipecat.
nodes.tradeoff: The talk calls real-time media quite challenging to scale, which is why it recommends these partners.

nodes.label: Live API session
nodes.detail: You open a session, then stream text, audio and video frames in over one websocket. The model streams audio chunks back as it answers.
nodes.tradeoff: A transcript of what was said comes back alongside the audio, even though the model itself never goes through text.

nodes.label: Native audio model
nodes.detail: The same model behind voice in the Gemini app. Its intelligence is built into the audio model, so it understands speech natively instead of reading a transcript.
nodes.tradeoff: Working in audio lets it switch fluidly between the 90 languages supported in preview, mid-conversation.

nodes.label: Function calls
nodes.detail: The model can call functions while talking. The radio DJ demo calls Lyria 3 to make a song on request; in a business it could fetch CRM data or open a ticket.
nodes.tradeoff: Generative tools are not instant: an image generated through a tool call still took two to three seconds.

nodes.label: Search grounding
nodes.detail: Turned on with one setting, it works like a built-in function call: the model goes off and searches, for example for today's weather.
nodes.tradeoff: The model knows a lot from training but has no real-time information; grounding fills that gap.

nodes.label: Chained pipeline
nodes.detail: The traditional voice agent: transcribe, send text to an LLM, call tools, generate text, turn it into audio. ChatGPT's first two voice modes were built this way.
nodes.tradeoff: Those chained modes had significantly higher latency than the native-audio Advanced Voice Mode.

flow.text: Asks the radio DJ agent for a high-energy reggaeton track.
Streams the live microphone audio to the Live API.
Passes the audio over one open websocket, with no transcription step.
Understands the request in audio and decides to call the music tool.
Lyria 3 generates the song while the DJ announces it.
Streams reply audio chunks back, plus a transcript of what was said.
Hears the track and can barge in at any moment.

takeaways.text: Transcribing speech throws away tone, cadence, interruptions and background noise; a native audio model keeps that context.
Realtime models are trained on audio as tokens, and the industry is dropping strict turn-taking for continuous streaming.
When reasoning or tool calls add delay, prompt a short preamble so the agent says it is checking.
